available.quote: An applicant may secure a license to practice optometry in this state without taking all required examinations as follows: Presentation of a certified copy or an original certificate of registration or license in good standing issued to the applicant by another state where the requirements for license are equivalent to those of this state

requirements.value: License in good standing from another state with equivalent requirements; apply for highest level of therapeutic licensure; current in CE requirements of current state; pass ND state optometry law examination (unless waived); minimum four years practice/federal service/teaching experience; no grounds for disciplinary action; oral interview before board.
requirements.quote: Unless waived by the board, all applicants for licensure by endorsement must: a. Apply for the highest level of therapeutic licensure in this state. b. Be current in the continuing education requirements of their current state of licensure. c. Pass a North Dakota state optometry law examination... d. Have a minimum of four years of practice, federal service, or teaching experience... e. Have not committed any act that would constitute grounds for disciplinary action... f. Submit to an oral interview

definition_quote.value: "Diagnosis and treatment" means the determination, interpretation, and treatment of any visual, muscular, neurological, interpretative, or anatomical anomaly of the eye which may be aided, relieved, or corrected through visual training procedures or through the use of lenses, prisms, filters, ophthalmic instruments, pharmaceutical agents, or combinations thereof, held either in contact with the eye, or in frames or mountings, as further authorized by this chapter. Laser therapy and the use of invasive surgery are not permitted under this chapter, except superficial foreign bodies may be removed and primary care procedures may be performed.

drug_authority.value: Optometrists certified by the board may prescribe and use pharmaceutical agents including diagnostic and therapeutic agents (topical, locally administered, oral anti-infectives, antihistaminics, and oral analgesics). Optometrists may not dispense therapeutic pharmaceutical agents except as drug samples or selling contact lenses/ophthalmic devices classified as drugs by FDA.
drug_authority.quote: "Pharmaceutical agent" means diagnostic pharmaceutical agents or therapeutic pharmaceutical agents. The term includes nonscheduled pharmaceutical agents, except for acetaminophen with thirty milligrams of codeine, that have documented use in the treatment of ocular-related disorders or diseases.
